key_insight: This paper studies when calibration actually helps mixture-of-experts models, especially under distribution shift. The main takeaway is that calibrated experts can improve both uncertainty quality and performance, but only under certain conditions that the paper aims to characterize.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of understanding around when enforcing calibration on individual experts improves mixture-of-experts models, particularly when the test data distribution differs from training.
method: Analyze mixture-of-experts behavior through the lens of calibration at the individual expert level.
Study how distribution shift changes the relationship between calibration, expert selection, and ensemble performance.
Identify conditions under which calibrated experts lead to better uncertainty estimates and stronger predictive results.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this helps decide when calibration is worth enforcing in MoE systems and when it may not help. That can lead to more reliable uncertainty estimates and more trustworthy deployed models under real-world shift.
visual_elements: A MoE pipeline diagram showing gating, experts, and calibration feedback
Side-by-side comparison of calibrated vs. uncalibrated expert predictions under distribution shift
A reliability diagram or calibration curve
A flowchart summarizing when calibration helps or fails
paper_title: Toward Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Under Distribution Shift
paper_authors: Gina Wong, Drew Prinster, Suchi Saria, Rama Chellappa, Anqi Liu
